intro_html: Salsa verde does the heavy lifting here, so you get bright, tangy pork with almost no effort. It stacks up 55 grams of protein per bowl over rice and corn, all for right around $3.96 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one batch is a whole lot of lunch for the money.
cost_closing_html: About $3.96 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: You are looking at about 579 calories and 55 grams of protein in every serving.
upsell_html: One quiet afternoon of cooking buys you a week of bowls you will actually look forward to. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Pork tenderloin runs lean and clean, but watch the tag. If it is over $4 a pound, check for pork loin instead and save real money on the same batch.
A single jar of salsa verde does most of the seasoning, so you skip buying a handful of separate spices.
Buy lime juice in a bottle rather than fresh limes for batch cooking. It keeps in the fridge and you only use a splash.
make_it: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Pour the salsa verde, diced green chiles, and chicken broth over the top.
Add a squeeze of lime juice and the minced garlic.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork and stir it back into all those juices, then fold in the corn.
Spoon over cooked white rice and divide into containers.
